note: One entry per competition actually entered. This is the file that makes win-prediction possible later, and nothing can generate it automatically - a commit log cannot tell you that three hours went to a broken auth flow, or that the idea was chosen in the last 48 hours. Write it within a day of the event, while it is still true. Until roughly 5-8 entries exist, the board deliberately shows no win-probability model (see docs/ROADMAP.md); one outcome cannot train anything, and a confident number from one data point is worse than no number.

schema.opportunity_id: matches data/opportunities.json, or null if the board never tracked it
schema.idea_origin: where the idea came from - prior build, the brief itself, a reused component
schema.outcome: won | placed | finalist | entered | rejected | withdrew | missed
schema.what_cost_us: the thing that actually burned time or points
would_reuse: components/approaches worth carrying into the next one
schema.judge_feedback: verbatim if we got any - never paraphrased into something flattering

retros._note: Skeleton only. Verified: Vuka (15 Jul) was the theme/idea/plan submitted to apply; BEACON (24-27 Jul) was the practice build; placed Top 6. Every null is a real gap only the two of you can fill.
retros._worth_capturing: The apply-then-practise sequence is itself the most interesting thing here, and it is the one pattern with a known good outcome attached. Worth recording deliberately: how the Vuka idea was chosen, why BEACON was the practice target, and whether practising in HTML while submitting in Python helped or split focus. That is the reusable play, and no commit log contains it.
